result:
The proposed answer of 0 depends on the claim that every positive integer is the cardinality of some finite partisan misère quotient. The solution gives no construction or argument for this. It only says partisan games are "flexible enough".

The question asks for the sum of the positive integers that cannot be realized. That wording implies a nonempty set of exceptions, so an empty sum of 0 is unlikely. I also vaguely recall that the literature on misère quotients shows some small orders are impossible. I could not recall which orders or verify this from memory.

The order-2 case in the solution is also not established. It simply asserts that the monoid {0, *} with * + * = 0 is realized, without checking it against the indistinguishability definition.

Since the key claim is unsupported and likely wrong, I cannot accept the answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
